adherence.reason: The piece is presented as historical fiction, grounding its invented nurse and village hospital in the 1918 influenza pandemic.
Elara is explicitly a volunteer nurse tending an overcrowded field hospital in October 1918 during the influenza outbreak.
She privately writes patients' names in the crowded margins of a hymn book and rejects reducing them to mortality data.
The hospital runs out of gauze and the main sequence marks a full thirty-six-hour shift, but a substantial dusk-and-night episode occurs before the text announces that the shift begins.
The narration is overwhelmingly in present tense, but it contains an explicit past-tense slip in 'their breath finally stilled.'
Elara conceals worsening fever, dizziness, chest constriction, and a wet cough, covering the cough and insisting she cannot leave the patients.
The final action is Elara collapsing from fever as the incoming relief women arrive and one reaches to catch her.
